blocks.text:
# gh-1073: Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash

## Description

## Session file grows unboundedly (12 GiB) → resume fails with `SessionException: Failed to read session`, then Dart VM OOM crash

### Observed (live, 2026-09-29)

A month-long CLI session (`2026-09-07…01a07bce-….jsonl`) grew to **12.4 GiB / 96,776 lines**. Messages themselves are only ~17 MB; 99.9 % of the file is `custom` ledger records:

| customType | records | total | avg |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model_request_summary` | 18,753 | 9.08 GB | ~484 KB |
| `shell_job_registry` | 29,348 | 3.65 GB | ~124 KB |
| `subagent_registry` | 3,588 | 0.5 GB | ~140 KB |

Resuming the session fails:

```
error: failed to open session 01a07bce-…: SessionException: Failed to read session …/2026-09-07…_01a07bce….jsonl
```

and the process then crashes hard:

```
Exhausted heap space, trying to allocate 25575341936 bytes
```

### Root cause

1. **Unbounded append-only ledgers.**
   - `shell_job_registry` (`lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart`, `_persistJobBoard`): every job-board mutation appends a **full snapshot of all job cards** (commands, cwd, log tails). ~29k snapshots over the session lifetime; no cap, no dedup, no rotation.
   - `model_request_summary` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_blobs.dart`): written before **every** model request and embeds a per-message summary of the whole outbound context (`messageCount` reached 1030+). Growth is superlinear: the longer the session, the bigger each record.

2. **Open path reads the whole file into one String.**
   `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart`) calls `fs.readTextFile(filePath)` on the entire JSONL. A 12.4 GiB UTF-8 file becomes a Dart UTF-16 `String` (~25 GB) → heap exhaustion; the wrapped `Failed to read session` error surfaces first, the retry then kills the VM.

   Note: faster/bounded parsing already exists (`SessionParseExecutor` header-only decode for big ledger payloads, `windowed_session_storage.dart`), but it only kicks in **after** the full-file `readTextFile`, so it cannot help here.

### Suggested fix directions

- **Streamed/windowed open**: read the JSONL line-by-line (or in bounded chunks) during open; never materialize the whole file as a single `String`. The header parse already only needs the first line.
- **Cap/rotate ledger records**:
  - `shell_job_registry`: keep only the latest snapshot (supersede prior records, e.g. tombstone/compact or a sidecar), or truncate job card payloads (log tails) before persisting.
  - `model_request_summary`: cap the per-message summary (max messages / max chars), and/or persist it only when the trajectory actually needs replay data.
- **Hard backstop**: refuse to full-read session files above a threshold (e.g. 1–2 GB) with a clear error pointing at a repair/`--shallow` resume path, instead of OOM-crashing.
- **Repair path**: a tool/command that rewrites a bloated JSONL, dropping or trimming `custom` ledgers, so users can rescue long-running sessions.

### Workaround for affected users

Copy the JSONL, strip `custom`-type lines (they are not needed to resume the conversation itself), and resume the copy — or start a new session.

blocks.text:
# gh-1073: Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash

## Description

## Session file grows unboundedly (12 GiB) → resume fails with `SessionException: Failed to read session`, then Dart VM OOM crash

### Observed (live, 2026-09-29)

A month-long CLI session (`2026-09-07…01a07bce-….jsonl`) grew to **12.4 GiB / 96,776 lines**. Messages themselves are only ~17 MB; 99.9 % of the file is `custom` ledger records:

| customType | records | total | avg |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model_request_summary` | 18,753 | 9.08 GB | ~484 KB |
| `shell_job_registry` | 29,348 | 3.65 GB | ~124 KB |
| `subagent_registry` | 3,588 | 0.5 GB | ~140 KB |

Resuming the session fails:

```
error: failed to open session 01a07bce-…: SessionException: Failed to read session …/2026-09-07…_01a07bce….jsonl
```

and the process then crashes hard:

```
Exhausted heap space, trying to allocate 25575341936 bytes
```

### Root cause

1. **Unbounded append-only ledgers.**
   - `shell_job_registry` (`lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart`, `_persistJobBoard`): every job-board mutation appends a **full snapshot of all job cards** (commands, cwd, log tails). ~29k snapshots over the session lifetime; no cap, no dedup, no rotation.
   - `model_request_summary` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_blobs.dart`): written before **every** model request and embeds a per-message summary of the whole outbound context (`messageCount` reached 1030+). Growth is superlinear: the longer the session, the bigger each record.

2. **Open path reads the whole file into one String.**
   `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart`) calls `fs.readTextFile(filePath)` on the entire JSONL. A 12.4 GiB UTF-8 file becomes a Dart UTF-16 `String` (~25 GB) → heap exhaustion; the wrapped `Failed to read session` error surfaces first, the retry then kills the VM.

   Note: faster/bounded parsing already exists (`SessionParseExecutor` header-only decode for big ledger payloads, `windowed_session_storage.dart`), but it only kicks in **after** the full-file `readTextFile`, so it cannot help here.

### Suggested fix directions

- **Streamed/windowed open**: read the JSONL line-by-line (or in bounded chunks) during open; never materialize the whole file as a single `String`. The header parse already only needs the first line.
- **Cap/rotate ledger records**:
  - `shell_job_registry`: keep only the latest snapshot (supersede prior records, e.g. tombstone/compact or a sidecar), or truncate job card payloads (log tails) before persisting.
  - `model_request_summary`: cap the per-message summary (max messages / max chars), and/or persist it only when the trajectory actually needs replay data.
- **Hard backstop**: refuse to full-read session files above a threshold (e.g. 1–2 GB) with a clear error pointing at a repair/`--shallow` resume path, instead of OOM-crashing.
- **Repair path**: a tool/command that rewrites a bloated JSONL, dropping or trimming `custom` ledgers, so users can rescue long-running sessions.

### Workaround for affected users

Copy the JSONL, strip `custom`-type lines (they are not needed to resume the conversation itself), and resume the copy — or start a new session.

1. **Unbounded append-only ledgers.**
   - `shell_job_registry` (`lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart`, `_persistJobBoard`): every job-board mutation appends a **full snapshot of all job cards** (commands, cwd, log tails). ~29k snapshots over the session lifetime; no cap, no dedup, no rotation.
   - `model_request_summary` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_blobs.dart`): written before **every** model request and embeds a per-message summary of the whole outbound context (`messageCount` reached 1030+). Growth is superlinear: the longer the session, the bigger each record.

2. **Open path reads the whole file into one String.**
   `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart`) calls `fs.readTextFile(filePath)` on the entire JSONL. A 12.4 GiB UTF-8 file becomes a Dart UTF-16 `String` (~25 GB) → heap exhaustion; the wrapped `Failed to read session` error surfaces first, the retry then kills the VM.

   Note: faster/bounded parsing already exists (`SessionParseExecutor` header-only decode for big ledger payloads, `windowed_session_storage.dart`), but it only kicks in **after** the full-file `readTextFile`, so it cannot help here.

### Suggested fix directions

- **Streamed/windowed open**: read the JSONL line-by-line (or in bounded chunks) during open; never materialize the whole file as a single `String`. The header parse already only needs the first line.
- **Cap/rotate ledger records**:
  - `shell_job_registry`: keep only the latest snapshot (supersede prior records, e.g. tombstone/compact or a sidecar), or truncate job card payloads (log tails) before persisting.
  - `model_request_summary`: cap the per-message summary (max messages / max chars), and/or persist it only when the trajectory actually needs replay data.
- **Hard backstop**: refuse to full-read session files above a threshold (e.g. 1–2 GB) with a clear error pointing at a repair/`--shallow` resume path, instead of OOM-crashing.
- **Repair path**: a tool/command that rewrites a bloated JSONL, dropping or trimming `custom` ledgers, so users can rescue long-running sessions.

### Workaround for affected users

Copy the JSONL, strip `custom`-type lines (they are not needed to resume the conversation itself), and resume the copy — or start a new session.

blocks.text:
# gh-1073: Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash

## Description

## Session file grows unboundedly (12 GiB) → resume fails with `SessionException: Failed to read session`, then Dart VM OOM crash

### Observed (live, 2026-09-29)

A month-long CLI session (`2026-09-07…01a07bce-….jsonl`) grew to **12.4 GiB / 96,776 lines**. Messages themselves are only ~17 MB; 99.9 % of the file is `custom` ledger records:

| customType | records | total | avg |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model_request_summary` | 18,753 | 9.08 GB | ~484 KB |
| `shell_job_registry` | 29,348 | 3.65 GB | ~124 KB |
| `subagent_registry` | 3,588 | 0.5 GB | ~140 KB |

Resuming the session fails:

```
error: failed to open session 01a07bce-…: SessionException: Failed to read session …/2026-09-07…_01a07bce….jsonl
```

and the process then crashes hard:

```
Exhausted heap space, trying to allocate 25575341936 bytes
```

### Root cause

1. **Unbounded append-only ledgers.**
   - `shell_job_registry` (`lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart`, `_persistJobBoard`): every job-board mutation appends a **full snapshot of all job cards** (commands, cwd, log tails). ~29k snapshots over the session lifetime; no cap, no dedup, no rotation.
   - `model_request_summary` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_blobs.dart`): written before **every** model request and embeds a per-message summary of the whole outbound context (`messageCount` reached 1030+). Growth is superlinear: the longer the session, the bigger each record.

2. **Open path reads the whole file into one String.**
   `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart`) calls `fs.readTextFile(filePath)` on the entire JSONL. A 12.4 GiB UTF-8 file becomes a Dart UTF-16 `String` (~25 GB) → heap exhaustion; the wrapped `Failed to read session` error surfaces first, the retry then kills the VM.

   Note: faster/bounded parsing already exists (`SessionParseExecutor` header-only decode for big ledger payloads, `windowed_session_storage.dart`), but it only kicks in **after** the full-file `readTextFile`, so it cannot help here.

### Suggested fix directions

- **Streamed/windowed open**: read the JSONL line-by-line (or in bounded chunks) during open; never materialize the whole file as a single `String`. The header parse already only needs the first line.
- **Cap/rotate ledger records**:
  - `shell_job_registry`: keep only the latest snapshot (supersede prior records, e.g. tombstone/compact or a sidecar), or truncate job card payloads (log tails) before persisting.
  - `model_request_summary`: cap the per-message summary (max messages / max chars), and/or persist it only when the trajectory actually needs replay data.
- **Hard backstop**: refuse to full-read session files above a threshold (e.g. 1–2 GB) with a clear error pointing at a repair/`--shallow` resume path, instead of OOM-crashing.
- **Repair path**: a tool/command that rewrites a bloated JSONL, dropping or trimming `custom` ledgers, so users can rescue long-running sessions.

### Workaround for affected users

Copy the JSONL, strip `custom`-type lines (they are not needed to resume the conversation itself), and resume the copy — or start a new session.

   - `shell_job_registry` (`lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart`, `_persistJobBoard`): every job-board mutation appends a **full snapshot of all job cards** (commands, cwd, log tails). ~29k snapshots over the session lifetime; no cap, no dedup, no rotation.
   - `model_request_summary` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_blobs.dart`): written before **every** model request and embeds a per-message summary of the whole outbound context (`messageCount` reached 1030+). Growth is superlinear: the longer the session, the bigger each record.

2. **Open path reads the whole file into one String.**
   `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart`) calls `fs.readTextFile(filePath)` on the entire JSONL. A 12.4 GiB UTF-8 file becomes a Dart UTF-16 `String` (~25 GB) → heap exhaustion; the wrapped `Failed to read session` error surfaces first, the retry then kills the VM.

   Note: faster/bounded parsing already exists (`SessionParseExecutor` header-only decode for big ledger payloads, `windowed_session_storage.dart`), but it only kicks in **after** the full-file `readTextFile`, so it cannot help here.

### Suggested fix directions

- **Streamed/windowed open**: read the JSONL line-by-line (or in bounded chunks) during open; never materialize the whole file as a single `String`. The header parse already only needs the first line.
- **Cap/rotate ledger records**:
  - `shell_job_registry`: keep only the latest snapshot (supersede prior records, e.g. tombstone/compact or a sidecar), or truncate job card payloads (log tails) before persisting.
  - `model_request_summary`: cap the per-message summary (max messages / max chars), and/or persist it only when the trajectory actually needs replay data.
- **Hard backstop**: refuse to full-read session files above a threshold (e.g. 1–2 GB) with a clear error pointing at a repair/`--shallow` resume path, instead of OOM-crashing.
- **Repair path**: a tool/command that rewrites a bloated JSONL, dropping or trimming `custom` ledgers, so users can rescue long-running sessions.

### Workaround for affected users

Copy the JSONL, strip `custom`-type lines (they are not needed to resume the conversation itself), and resume the copy — or start a new session.

# gh-1073: Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash

## Description

## Session file grows unboundedly (12 GiB) → resume fails with `SessionException: Failed to read session`, then Dart VM OOM crash

### Observed (live, 2026-09-29)

A month-long CLI session (`2026-09-07…01a07bce-….jsonl`) grew to **12.4 GiB / 96,776 lines**. Messages themselves are only ~17 MB; 99.9 % of the file is `custom` ledger records:

| customType | records | total | avg |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model_request_summary` | 18,753 | 9.08 GB | ~484 KB |
| `shell_job_registry` | 29,348 | 3.65 GB | ~124 KB |
| `subagent_registry` | 3,588 | 0.5 GB | ~140 KB |

Resuming the session fails:

```
error: failed to open session 01a07bce-…: SessionException: Failed to read session …/2026-09-07…_01a07bce….jsonl
```

and the process then crashes hard:

```
Exhausted heap space, trying to allocate 25575341936 bytes
```

### Root cause

1. **Unbounded append-only ledgers.**
   - `shell_job_registry` (`lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart`, `_persistJobBoard`): every job-board mutation appends a **full snapshot of all job cards** (commands, cwd, log tails). ~29k snapshots over the session lifetime; no cap, no dedup, no rotation.
   - `model_request_summary` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_blobs.dart`): written before **every** model request and embeds a per-message summary of the whole outbound context (`messageCount` reached 1030+). Growth is superlinear: the longer the session, the bigger each record.

2. **Open path reads the whole file into one String.**
   `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart`) calls `fs.readTextFile(filePath)` on the entire JSONL. A 12.4 GiB UTF-8 file becomes a Dart UTF-16 `String` (~25 GB) → heap exhaustion; the wrapped `Failed to read session` error surfaces first, the retry then kills the VM.

   Note: faster/bounded parsing already exists (`SessionParseExecutor` header-only decode for big ledger payloads, `windowed_session_storage.dart`), but it only kicks in **after** the full-file `readTextFile`, so it cannot help here.

### Suggested fix directions

- **Streamed/windowed open**: read the JSONL line-by-line (or in bounded chunks) during open; never materialize the whole file as a single `String`. The header parse already only needs the first line.
- **Cap/rotate ledger records**:
  - `shell_job_registry`: keep only the latest snapshot (supersede prior records, e.g. tombstone/compact or a sidecar), or truncate job card payloads (log tails) before persisting.
  - `model_request_summary`: cap the per-message summary (max messages / max chars), and/or persist it only when the trajectory actually needs replay data.
- **Hard backstop**: refuse to full-read session files above a threshold (e.g. 1–2 GB) with a clear error pointing at a repair/`--shallow` resume path, instead of OOM-crashing.
- **Repair path**: a tool/command that rewrites a bloated JSONL, dropping or trimming `custom` ledgers, so users can rescue long-running sessions.

### Workaround for affected users

Copy the JSONL, strip `custom`-type lines (they are not needed to resume the conversation itself), and resume the copy — or start a new session.

# gh-1073: Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash

## Description

## Session file grows unboundedly (12 GiB) → resume fails with `SessionException: Failed to read session`, then Dart VM OOM crash

### Observed (live, 2026-09-29)

A month-long CLI session (`2026-09-07…01a07bce-….jsonl`) grew to **12.4 GiB / 96,776 lines**. Messages themselves are only ~17 MB; 99.9 % of the file is `custom` ledger records:

| customType | records | total | avg |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model_request_summary` | 18,753 | 9.08 GB | ~484 KB |
| `shell_job_registry` | 29,348 | 3.65 GB | ~124 KB |
| `subagent_registry` | 3,588 | 0.5 GB | ~140 KB |

Resuming the session fails:

```
error: failed to open session 01a07bce-…: SessionException: Failed to read session …/2026-09-07…_01a07bce….jsonl
```

and the process then crashes hard:

```
Exhausted heap space, trying to allocate 25575341936 bytes
```

### Root cause

1. **Unbounded append-only ledgers.**
   - `shell_job_registry` (`lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart`, `_persistJobBoard`): every job-board mutation appends a **full snapshot of all job cards** (commands, cwd, log tails). ~29k snapshots over the session lifetime; no cap, no dedup, no rotation.
   - `model_request_summary` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_blobs.dart`): written before **every** model request and embeds a per-message summary of the whole outbound context (`messageCount` reached 1030+). Growth is superlinear: the longer the session, the bigger each record.

2. **Open path reads the whole file into one String.**
   `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart`) calls `fs.readTextFile(filePath)` on the entire JSONL. A 12.4 GiB UTF-8 file becomes a Dart UTF-16 `String` (~25 GB) → heap exhaustion; the wrapped `Failed to read session` error surfaces first, the retry then kills the VM.

   Note: faster/bounded parsing already exists (`SessionParseExecutor` header-only decode for big ledger payloads, `windowed_session_storage.dart`), but it only kicks in **after** the full-file `readTextFile`, so it cannot help here.

### Suggested fix directions

- **Streamed/windowed open**: read the JSONL line-by-line (or in bounded chunks) during open; never materialize the whole file as a single `String`. The header parse already only needs the first line.
- **Cap/rotate ledger records**:
  - `shell_job_registry`: keep only the latest snapshot (supersede prior records, e.g. tombstone/compact or a sidecar), or truncate job card payloads (log tails) before persisting.
  - `model_request_summary`: cap the per-message summary (max messages / max chars), and/or persist it only when the trajectory actually needs replay data.
- **Hard backstop**: refuse to full-read session files above a threshold (e.g. 1–2 GB) with a clear error pointing at a repair/`--shallow` resume path, instead of OOM-crashing.
- **Repair path**: a tool/command that rewrites a bloated JSONL, dropping or trimming `custom` ledgers, so users can rescue long-running sessions.

### Workaround for affected users

Copy the JSONL, strip `custom`-type lines (they are not needed to resume the conversation itself), and resume the copy — or start a new session.

## Session file grows unboundedly (12 GiB) → resume fails with `SessionException: Failed to read session`, then Dart VM OOM crash

### Observed (live, 2026-09-29)

A month-long CLI session (`2026-09-07…01a07bce-….jsonl`) grew to **12.4 GiB / 96,776 lines**. Messages themselves are only ~17 MB; 99.9 % of the file is `custom` ledger records:

| customType | records | total | avg |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model_request_summary` | 18,753 | 9.08 GB | ~484 KB |
| `shell_job_registry` | 29,348 | 3.65 GB | ~124 KB |
| `subagent_registry` | 3,588 | 0.5 GB | ~140 KB |

Resuming the session fails:

```
error: failed to open session 01a07bce-…: SessionException: Failed to read session …/2026-09-07…_01a07bce….jsonl
```

and the process then crashes hard:

```
Exhausted heap space, trying to allocate 25575341936 bytes
```

### Root cause

1. **Unbounded append-only ledgers.**
   - `shell_job_registry` (`lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart`, `_persistJobBoard`): every job-board mutation appends a **full snapshot of all job cards** (commands, cwd, log tails). ~29k snapshots over the session lifetime; no cap, no dedup, no rotation.
   - `model_request_summary` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_blobs.dart`): written before **every** model request and embeds a per-message summary of the whole outbound context (`messageCount` reached 1030+). Growth is superlinear: the longer the session, the bigger each record.

2. **Open path reads the whole file into one String.**
   `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart`) calls `fs.readTextFile(filePath)` on the entire JSONL. A 12.4 GiB UTF-8 file becomes a Dart UTF-16 `String` (~25 GB) → heap exhaustion; the wrapped `Failed to read session` error surfaces first, the retry then kills the VM.

   Note: faster/bounded parsing already exists (`SessionParseExecutor` header-only decode for big ledger payloads, `windowed_session_storage.dart`), but it only kicks in **after** the full-file `readTextFile`, so it cannot help here.

### Suggested fix directions

- **Streamed/windowed open**: read the JSONL line-by-line (or in bounded chunks) during open; never materialize the whole file as a single `String`. The header parse already only needs the first line.
- **Cap/rotate ledger records**:
  - `shell_job_registry`: keep only the latest snapshot (supersede prior records, e.g. tombstone/compact or a sidecar), or truncate job card payloads (log tails) before persisting.
  - `model_request_summary`: cap the per-message summary (max messages / max chars), and/or persist it only when the trajectory actually needs replay data.
- **Hard backstop**: refuse to full-read session files above a threshold (e.g. 1–2 GB) with a clear error pointing at a repair/`--shallow` resume path, instead of OOM-crashing.
- **Repair path**: a tool/command that rewrites a bloated JSONL, dropping or trimming `custom` ledgers, so users can rescue long-running sessions.

### Workaround for affected users

Copy the JSONL, strip `custom`-type lines (they are not needed to resume the conversation itself), and resume the copy — or start a new session.

# gh-1073: Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash

## Description

## Session file grows unboundedly (12 GiB) → resume fails with `SessionException: Failed to read session`, then Dart VM OOM crash

### Observed (live, 2026-09-29)

A month-long CLI session (`2026-09-07…01a07bce-….jsonl`) grew to **12.4 GiB / 96,776 lines**. Messages themselves are only ~17 MB; 99.9 % of the file is `custom` ledger records:

| customType | records | total | avg |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model_request_summary` | 18,753 | 9.08 GB | ~484 KB |
| `shell_job_registry` | 29,348 | 3.65 GB | ~124 KB |
| `subagent_registry` | 3,588 | 0.5 GB | ~140 KB |

Resuming the session fails:

```
error: failed to open session 01a07bce-…: SessionException: Failed to read session …/2026-09-07…_01a07bce….jsonl
```

and the process then crashes hard:

```
Exhausted heap space, trying to allocate 25575341936 bytes
```

### Root cause

1. **Unbounded append-only ledgers.**
   - `shell_job_registry` (`lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart`, `_persistJobBoard`): every job-board mutation appends a **full snapshot of all job cards** (commands, cwd, log tails). ~29k snapshots over the session lifetime; no cap, no dedup, no rotation.
   - `model_request_summary` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_blobs.dart`): written before **every** model request and embeds a per-message summary of the whole outbound context (`messageCount` reached 1030+). Growth is superlinear: the longer the session, the bigger each record.

2. **Open path reads the whole file into one String.**
   `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart`) calls `fs.readTextFile(filePath)` on the entire JSONL. A 12.4 GiB UTF-8 file becomes a Dart UTF-16 `String` (~25 GB) → heap exhaustion; the wrapped `Failed to read session` error surfaces first, the retry then kills the VM.

   Note: faster/bounded parsing already exists (`SessionParseExecutor` header-only decode for big ledger payloads, `windowed_session_storage.dart`), but it only kicks in **after** the full-file `readTextFile`, so it cannot help here.

### Suggested fix directions

- **Streamed/windowed open**: read the JSONL line-by-line (or in bounded chunks) during open; never materialize the whole file as a single `String`. The header parse already only needs the first line.
- **Cap/rotate ledger records**:
  - `shell_job_registry`: keep only the latest snapshot (supersede prior records, e.g. tombstone/compact or a sidecar), or truncate job card payloads (log tails) before persisting.
  - `model_request_summary`: cap the per-message summary (max messages / max chars), and/or persist it only when the trajectory actually needs replay data.
- **Hard backstop**: refuse to full-read session files above a threshold (e.g. 1–2 GB) with a clear error pointing at a repair/`--shallow` resume path, instead of OOM-crashing.
- **Repair path**: a tool/command that rewrites a bloated JSONL, dropping or trimming `custom` ledgers, so users can rescue long-running sessions.

### Workaround for affected users

Copy the JSONL, strip `custom`-type lines (they are not needed to resume the conversation itself), and resume the copy — or start a new session.

# gh-1073: Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash

## Description

## Session file grows unboundedly (12 GiB) → resume fails with `SessionException: Failed to read session`, then Dart VM OOM crash

### Observed (live, 2026-09-29)

A month-long CLI session (`2026-09-07…01a07bce-….jsonl`) grew to **12.4 GiB / 96,776 lines**. Messages themselves are only ~17 MB; 99.9 % of the file is `custom` ledger records:

| customType | records | total | avg |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model_request_summary` | 18,753 | 9.08 GB | ~484 KB |
| `shell_job_registry` | 29,348 | 3.65 GB | ~124 KB |
| `subagent_registry` | 3,588 | 0.5 GB | ~140 KB |

Resuming the session fails:

```
error: failed to open session 01a07bce-…: SessionException: Failed to read session …/2026-09-07…_01a07bce….jsonl
```

and the process then crashes hard:

```
Exhausted heap space, trying to allocate 25575341936 bytes
```

### Root cause

1. **Unbounded append-only ledgers.**
   - `shell_job_registry` (`lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart`, `_persistJobBoard`): every job-board mutation appends a **full snapshot of all job cards** (commands, cwd, log tails). ~29k snapshots over the session lifetime; no cap, no dedup, no rotation.
   - `model_request_summary` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_blobs.dart`): written before **every** model request and embeds a per-message summary of the whole outbound context (`messageCount` reached 1030+). Growth is superlinear: the longer the session, the bigger each record.

2. **Open path reads the whole file into one String.**
   `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart`) calls `fs.readTextFile(filePath)` on the entire JSONL. A 12.4 GiB UTF-8 file becomes a Dart UTF-16 `String` (~25 GB) → heap exhaustion; the wrapped `Failed to read session` error surfaces first, the retry then kills the VM.

   Note: faster/bounded parsing already exists (`SessionParseExecutor` header-only decode for big ledger payloads, `windowed_session_storage.dart`), but it only kicks in **after** the full-file `readTextFile`, so it cannot help here.

### Suggested fix directions

- **Streamed/windowed open**: read the JSONL line-by-line (or in bounded chunks) during open; never materialize the whole file as a single `String`. The header parse already only needs the first line.
- **Cap/rotate ledger records**:
  - `shell_job_registry`: keep only the latest snapshot (supersede prior records, e.g. tombstone/compact or a sidecar), or truncate job card payloads (log tails) before persisting.
  - `model_request_summary`: cap the per-message summary (max messages / max chars), and/or persist it only when the trajectory actually needs replay data.
- **Hard backstop**: refuse to full-read session files above a threshold (e.g. 1–2 GB) with a clear error pointing at a repair/`--shallow` resume path, instead of OOM-crashing.
- **Repair path**: a tool/command that rewrites a bloated JSONL, dropping or trimming `custom` ledgers, so users can rescue long-running sessions.

### Workaround for affected users

Copy the JSONL, strip `custom`-type lines (they are not needed to resume the conversation itself), and resume the copy — or start a new session.

blocks.text:
# gh-1073: Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash

## Description

## Session file grows unboundedly (12 GiB) → resume fails with `SessionException: Failed to read session`, then Dart VM OOM crash

### Observed (live, 2026-09-29)

A month-long CLI session (`2026-09-07…01a07bce-….jsonl`) grew to **12.4 GiB / 96,776 lines**. Messages themselves are only ~17 MB; 99.9 % of the file is `custom` ledger records:

| customType | records | total | avg |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model_request_summary` | 18,753 | 9.08 GB | ~484 KB |
| `shell_job_registry` | 29,348 | 3.65 GB | ~124 KB |
| `subagent_registry` | 3,588 | 0.5 GB | ~140 KB |

Resuming the session fails:

```
error: failed to open session 01a07bce-…: SessionException: Failed to read session …/2026-09-07…_01a07bce….jsonl
```

and the process then crashes hard:

```
Exhausted heap space, trying to allocate 25575341936 bytes
```

### Root cause

1. **Unbounded append-only ledgers.**
   - `shell_job_registry` (`lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart`, `_persistJobBoard`): every job-board mutation appends a **full snapshot of all job cards** (commands, cwd, log tails). ~29k snapshots over the session lifetime; no cap, no dedup, no rotation.
   - `model_request_summary` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_blobs.dart`): written before **every** model request and embeds a per-message summary of the whole outbound context (`messageCount` reached 1030+). Growth is superlinear: the longer the session, the bigger each record.

2. **Open path reads the whole file into one String.**
   `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart`) calls `fs.readTextFile(filePath)` on the entire JSONL. A 12.4 GiB UTF-8 file becomes a Dart UTF-16 `String` (~25 GB) → heap exhaustion; the wrapped `Failed to read session` error surfaces first, the retry then kills the VM.

   Note: faster/bounded parsing already exists (`SessionParseExecutor` header-only decode for big ledger payloads, `windowed_session_storage.dart`), but it only kicks in **after** the full-file `readTextFile`, so it cannot help here.

### Suggested fix directions

- **Streamed/windowed open**: read the JSONL line-by-line (or in bounded chunks) during open; never materialize the whole file as a single `String`. The header parse already only needs the first line.
- **Cap/rotate ledger records**:
  - `shell_job_registry`: keep only the latest snapshot (supersede prior records, e.g. tombstone/compact or a sidecar), or truncate job card payloads (log tails) before persisting.
  - `model_request_summary`: cap the per-message summary (max messages / max chars), and/or persist it only when the trajectory actually needs replay data.
- **Hard backstop**: refuse to full-read session files above a threshold (e.g. 1–2 GB) with a clear error pointing at a repair/`--shallow` resume path, instead of OOM-crashing.
- **Repair path**: a tool/command that rewrites a bloated JSONL, dropping or trimming `custom` ledgers, so users can rescue long-running sessions.

### Workaround for affected users

Copy the JSONL, strip `custom`-type lines (they are not needed to resume the conversation itself), and resume the copy — or start a new session.

    "description": "## Session file grows unboundedly (12 GiB) → resume fails with `SessionException: Failed to read session`, then Dart VM OOM crash

### Observed (live, 2026-09-29)

A month-long CLI session (`2026-09-07…01a07bce-….jsonl`) grew to **12.4 GiB / 96,776 lines**. Messages themselves are only ~17 MB; 99.9 % of the file is `custom` ledger records:

| customType | records | total | avg |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model_request_summary` | 18,753 | 9.08 GB | ~484 KB |
| `shell_job_registry` | 29,348 | 3.65 GB | ~124 KB |
| `subagent_registry` | 3,588 | 0.5 GB | ~140 KB |

Resuming the session fails:

```
error: failed to open session 01a07bce-…: SessionException: Failed to read session …/2026-09-07…_01a07bce….jsonl
```

and the process then crashes hard:

```
Exhausted heap space, trying to allocate 25575341936 bytes
```

### Root cause

1. **Unbounded append-only ledgers.**
   - `shell_job_registry` (`lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart`, `_persistJobBoard`): every job-board mutation appends a **full snapshot of all job cards** (commands, cwd, log tails). ~29k snapshots over the session lifetime; no cap, no dedup, no rotation.
   - `model_request_summary` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_blobs.dart`): written before **every** model request and embeds a per-message summary of the whole outbound context (`messageCount` reached 1030+). Growth is superlinear: the longer the session, the bigger each record.

2. **Open path reads the whole file into one String.**
   `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart`) calls `fs.readTextFile(filePath)` on the entire JSONL. A 12.4 GiB UTF-8 file becomes a Dart UTF-16 `String` (~25 GB) → heap exhaustion; the wrapped `Failed to read session` error surfaces first, the retry then kills the VM.

   Note: faster/bounded parsing already exists (`SessionParseExecutor` header-only decode for big ledger payloads, `windowed_session_storage.dart`), but it only kicks in **after** the full-file `readTextFile`, so it cannot help here.

### Suggested fix directions

- **Streamed/windowed open**: read the JSONL line-by-line (or in bounded chunks) during open; never materialize the whole file as a single `String`. The header parse already only needs the first line.
- **Cap/rotate ledger records**:
  - `shell_job_registry`: keep only the latest snapshot (supersede prior records, e.g. tombstone/compact or a sidecar), or truncate job card payloads (log tails) before persisting.
  - `model_request_summary`: cap the per-message summary (max messages / max chars), and/or persist it only when the trajectory actually needs replay data.
- **Hard backstop**: refuse to full-read session files above a threshold (e.g. 1–2 GB) with a clear error pointing at a repair/`--shallow` resume path, instead of OOM-crashing.
- **Repair path**: a tool/command that rewrites a bloated JSONL, dropping or trimming `custom` ledgers, so users can rescue long-running sessions.

### Workaround for affected users

Copy the JSONL, strip `custom`-type lines (they are not needed to resume the conversation itself), and resume the copy — or start a new session.

# gh-1073: Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash

## Description

## Session file grows unboundedly (12 GiB) → resume fails with `SessionException: Failed to read session`, then Dart VM OOM crash

### Observed (live, 2026-09-29)

A month-long CLI session (`2026-09-07…01a07bce-….jsonl`) grew to **12.4 GiB / 96,776 lines**. Messages themselves are only ~17 MB; 99.9 % of the file is `custom` ledger records:

| customType | records | total | avg |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model_request_summary` | 18,753 | 9.08 GB | ~484 KB |
| `shell_job_registry` | 29,348 | 3.65 GB | ~124 KB |
| `subagent_registry` | 3,588 | 0.5 GB | ~140 KB |

Resuming the session fails:

```
error: failed to open session 01a07bce-…: SessionException: Failed to read session …/2026-09-07…_01a07bce….jsonl
```

and the process then crashes hard:

```
Exhausted heap space, trying to allocate 25575341936 bytes
```

### Root cause

1. **Unbounded append-only ledgers.**
   - `shell_job_registry` (`lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart`, `_persistJobBoard`): every job-board mutation appends a **full snapshot of all job cards** (commands, cwd, log tails). ~29k snapshots over the session lifetime; no cap, no dedup, no rotation.
   - `model_request_summary` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_blobs.dart`): written before **every** model request and embeds a per-message summary of the whole outbound context (`messageCount` reached 1030+). Growth is superlinear: the longer the session, the bigger each record.

2. **Open path reads the whole file into one String.**
   `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart`) calls `fs.readTextFile(filePath)` on the entire JSONL. A 12.4 GiB UTF-8 file becomes a Dart UTF-16 `String` (~25 GB) → heap exhaustion; the wrapped `Failed to read session` error surfaces first, the retry then kills the VM.

   Note: faster/bounded parsing already exists (`SessionParseExecutor` header-only decode for big ledger payloads, `windowed_session_storage.dart`), but it only kicks in **after** the full-file `readTextFile`, so it cannot help here.

### Suggested fix directions

- **Streamed/windowed open**: read the JSONL line-by-line (or in bounded chunks) during open; never materialize the whole file as a single `String`. The header parse already only needs the first line.
- **Cap/rotate ledger records**:
  - `shell_job_registry`: keep only the latest snapshot (supersede prior records, e.g. tombstone/compact or a sidecar), or truncate job card payloads (log tails) before persisting.
  - `model_request_summary`: cap the per-message summary (max messages / max chars), and/or persist it only when the trajectory actually needs replay data.
- **Hard backstop**: refuse to full-read session files above a threshold (e.g. 1–2 GB) with a clear error pointing at a repair/`--shallow` resume path, instead of OOM-crashing.
- **Repair path**: a tool/command that rewrites a bloated JSONL, dropping or trimming `custom` ledgers, so users can rescue long-running sessions.

### Workaround for affected users

Copy the JSONL, strip `custom`-type lines (they are not needed to resume the conversation itself), and resume the copy — or start a new session.

### What changed Bounded the session-JSONL growth that grew a month-long session to 12.4 GiB and made open/resume safe for huge files: ledger payloads are capped and deduped at the write site, the full open streams the file in bounded chunks (never one giant `String`) with a 2 GiB hard backstop, and a new `fa session repair` command rewrites bloated JSONLs. This leg fixed the last review leftovers: one analyzer lint and two stale retry-test assertions that still counted the old `readTextFile` open surface (the open now stats + streams, so the counters read `statCalls`). ### Key decisions - `ledger_caps.dart`: 300-char cap on every string field in `shell_job_registry` / `subagent_registry` records + `LedgerSnapshotDeduper` skips byte-identical snapshots at the write site - `model_request_summary`: per-message summaries capped (newest 64 messages / 256 KB budget); older messages degrade to role+chars stubs — record still describes the whole request - `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked`: stat-first, refuse >2 GiB with a named `tooLarge` `SessionException` pointing at windowed resume / `fa session repair`; ranged filesystems get a fully streamed line-scan parse with header-only decode of giant `custom` ledgers (only the latest per `customType` is fully parsed — exactly what resume rehydration reads) - `session_repair.dart` + CLI: drop replay-only ledger types, keep-latest for snapshot registries, conservative (unknown/unparseable lines kept), backup + `--dry-run` ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/session test/trajectory test/task test/cli ``` Full core suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 7960 passed / 16 skipped. The 3 failures in `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` are environmental — the CI shell leaks `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, which the editor correctly refuses to override (all 13 pass with the var unset). A pre-existing glibc heap-corruption abort in the PTY-harness teardown also reproduces on the base commit and is unrelated.
Architecture diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD OPEN[Session open] --> STAT[fileInfo stat] STAT -->|> 2 GiB| REFUSE[tooLarge SessionException] REFUSE --> HINT[windowed resume / fa session repair] STAT -->|<= 2 GiB| STREAM[streamed line scan
bounded chunks] STREAM --> HDR[header-only decode
of giant custom ledgers] HDR --> LATEST[fully parse latest
record per customType] WRITE[ledger writes] --> CAP[ledger_caps: 300-char field cap] CAP --> DEDUP[skip identical snapshots] REPAIR[fa session repair] --> REWRITE[drop replay-only ledgers
keep-latest registries + backup] ```

# gh-1073: Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash

## Description

## Session file grows unboundedly (12 GiB) → resume fails with `SessionException: Failed to read session`, then Dart VM OOM crash

### Observed (live, 2026-09-29)

A month-long CLI session (`2026-09-07…01a07bce-….jsonl`) grew to **12.4 GiB / 96,776 lines**. Messages themselves are only ~17 MB; 99.9 % of the file is `custom` ledger records:

| customType | records | total | avg |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model_request_summary` | 18,753 | 9.08 GB | ~484 KB |
| `shell_job_registry` | 29,348 | 3.65 GB | ~124 KB |
| `subagent_registry` | 3,588 | 0.5 GB | ~140 KB |

Resuming the session fails:

```
error: failed to open session 01a07bce-…: SessionException: Failed to read session …/2026-09-07…_01a07bce….jsonl
```

and the process then crashes hard:

```
Exhausted heap space, trying to allocate 25575341936 bytes
```

### Root cause

1. **Unbounded append-only ledgers.**
   - `shell_job_registry` (`lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart`, `_persistJobBoard`): every job-board mutation appends a **full snapshot of all job cards** (commands, cwd, log tails). ~29k snapshots over the session lifetime; no cap, no dedup, no rotation.
   - `model_request_summary` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_blobs.dart`): written before **every** model request and embeds a per-message summary of the whole outbound context (`messageCount` reached 1030+). Growth is superlinear: the longer the session, the bigger each record.

2. **Open path reads the whole file into one String.**
   `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart`) calls `fs.readTextFile(filePath)` on the entire JSONL. A 12.4 GiB UTF-8 file becomes a Dart UTF-16 `String` (~25 GB) → heap exhaustion; the wrapped `Failed to read session` error surfaces first, the retry then kills the VM.

   Note: faster/bounded parsing already exists (`SessionParseExecutor` header-only decode for big ledger payloads, `windowed_session_storage.dart`), but it only kicks in **after** the full-file `readTextFile`, so it cannot help here.

### Suggested fix directions

- **Streamed/windowed open**: read the JSONL line-by-line (or in bounded chunks) during open; never materialize the whole file as a single `String`. The header parse already only needs the first line.
- **Cap/rotate ledger records**:
  - `shell_job_registry`: keep only the latest snapshot (supersede prior records, e.g. tombstone/compact or a sidecar), or truncate job card payloads (log tails) before persisting.
  - `model_request_summary`: cap the per-message summary (max messages / max chars), and/or persist it only when the trajectory actually needs replay data.
- **Hard backstop**: refuse to full-read session files above a threshold (e.g. 1–2 GB) with a clear error pointing at a repair/`--shallow` resume path, instead of OOM-crashing.
- **Repair path**: a tool/command that rewrites a bloated JSONL, dropping or trimming `custom` ledgers, so users can rescue long-running sessions.

### Workaround for affected users

Copy the JSONL, strip `custom`-type lines (they are not needed to resume the conversation itself), and resume the copy — or start a new session.

{"content":"### What changed Bounded the session-JSONL growth that grew a month-long session to 12.4 GiB and made open/resume safe for huge files: ledger payloads are capped and deduped at the write site, the full open streams the file in bounded chunks (never one giant `String`) with a 2 GiB hard backstop, and a new `fa session repair` command rewrites bloated JSONLs. This leg fixed the last review leftovers: one analyzer lint and two stale retry-test assertions that still counted the old `readTextFile` open surface (the open now stats + streams, so the counters read `statCalls`). ### Key decisions - `ledger_caps.dart`: 300-char cap on every string field in `shell_job_registry` / `subagent_registry` records + `LedgerSnapshotDeduper` skips byte-identical snapshots at the write site - `model_request_summary`: per-message summaries capped (newest 64 messages / 256 KB budget); older messages degrade to role+chars stubs — record still describes the whole request - `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked`: stat-first, refuse >2 GiB with a named `tooLarge` `SessionException` pointing at windowed resume / `fa session repair`; ranged filesystems get a fully streamed line-scan parse with header-only decode of giant `custom` ledgers (only the latest per `customType` is fully parsed — exactly what resume rehydration reads) - `session_repair.dart` + CLI: drop replay-only ledger types, keep-latest for snapshot registries, conservative (unknown/unparseable lines kept), backup + `--dry-run` ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/session test/trajectory test/task test/cli ``` Full core suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 7960 passed / 16 skipped. The 3 failures in `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` are environmental — the CI shell leaks `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, which the editor correctly refuses to override (all 13 pass with the var unset). A pre-existing glibc heap-corruption abort in the PTY-harness teardown also reproduces on the base commit and is unrelated.
Architecture diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD OPEN[Session open] --> STAT[fileInfo stat] STAT -->|> 2 GiB| REFUSE[tooLarge SessionException] REFUSE --> HINT[windowed resume / fa session repair] STAT -->|<= 2 GiB| STREAM[streamed line scan
bounded chunks] STREAM --> HDR[header-only decode
of giant custom ledgers] HDR --> LATEST[fully parse latest
record per customType] WRITE[ledger writes] --> CAP[ledger_caps: 300-char field cap] CAP --> DEDUP[skip identical snapshots] REPAIR[fa session repair] --> REWRITE[drop replay-only ledgers
keep-latest registries + backup] ```

blocks.text:
# gh-1073: Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash

## Description

## Session file grows unboundedly (12 GiB) → resume fails with `SessionException: Failed to read session`, then Dart VM OOM crash

### Observed (live, 2026-09-29)

A month-long CLI session (`2026-09-07…01a07bce-….jsonl`) grew to **12.4 GiB / 96,776 lines**. Messages themselves are only ~17 MB; 99.9 % of the file is `custom` ledger records:

| customType | records | total | avg |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model_request_summary` | 18,753 | 9.08 GB | ~484 KB |
| `shell_job_registry` | 29,348 | 3.65 GB | ~124 KB |
| `subagent_registry` | 3,588 | 0.5 GB | ~140 KB |

Resuming the session fails:

```
error: failed to open session 01a07bce-…: SessionException: Failed to read session …/2026-09-07…_01a07bce….jsonl
```

and the process then crashes hard:

```
Exhausted heap space, trying to allocate 25575341936 bytes
```

### Root cause

1. **Unbounded append-only ledgers.**
   - `shell_job_registry` (`lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart`, `_persistJobBoard`): every job-board mutation appends a **full snapshot of all job cards** (commands, cwd, log tails). ~29k snapshots over the session lifetime; no cap, no dedup, no rotation.
   - `model_request_summary` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_blobs.dart`): written before **every** model request and embeds a per-message summary of the whole outbound context (`messageCount` reached 1030+). Growth is superlinear: the longer the session, the bigger each record.

2. **Open path reads the whole file into one String.**
   `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart`) calls `fs.readTextFile(filePath)` on the entire JSONL. A 12.4 GiB UTF-8 file becomes a Dart UTF-16 `String` (~25 GB) → heap exhaustion; the wrapped `Failed to read session` error surfaces first, the retry then kills the VM.

   Note: faster/bounded parsing already exists (`SessionParseExecutor` header-only decode for big ledger payloads, `windowed_session_storage.dart`), but it only kicks in **after** the full-file `readTextFile`, so it cannot help here.

### Suggested fix directions

- **Streamed/windowed open**: read the JSONL line-by-line (or in bounded chunks) during open; never materialize the whole file as a single `String`. The header parse already only needs the first line.
- **Cap/rotate ledger records**:
  - `shell_job_registry`: keep only the latest snapshot (supersede prior records, e.g. tombstone/compact or a sidecar), or truncate job card payloads (log tails) before persisting.
  - `model_request_summary`: cap the per-message summary (max messages / max chars), and/or persist it only when the trajectory actually needs replay data.
- **Hard backstop**: refuse to full-read session files above a threshold (e.g. 1–2 GB) with a clear error pointing at a repair/`--shallow` resume path, instead of OOM-crashing.
- **Repair path**: a tool/command that rewrites a bloated JSONL, dropping or trimming `custom` ledgers, so users can rescue long-running sessions.

### Workaround for affected users

Copy the JSONL, strip `custom`-type lines (they are not needed to resume the conversation itself), and resume the copy — or start a new session.

A 12.4 GiB UTF-8 file becomes a Dart UTF-16 `String` (~25 GB) → heap exhaustion; the wrapped `Failed to read session` error surfaces first, the retry then kills the VM.

   Note: faster/bounded parsing already exists (`SessionParseExecutor` header-only decode for big ledger payloads, `windowed_session_storage.dart`), but it only kicks in **after** the full-file `readTextFile`, so it cannot help here.

### Suggested fix directions

- **Streamed/windowed open**: read the JSONL line-by-line (or in bounded chunks) during open; never materialize the whole file as a single `String`. The header parse already only needs the first line.
- **Cap/rotate ledger records**:
  - `shell_job_registry`: keep only the latest snapshot (supersede prior records, e.g. tombstone/compact or a sidecar), or truncate job card payloads (log tails) before persisting.
  - `model_request_summary`: cap the per-message summary (max messages / max chars), and/or persist it only when the trajectory actually needs replay data.
- **Hard backstop**: refuse to full-read session files above a threshold (e.g. 1–2 GB) with a clear error pointing at a repair/`--shallow` resume path, instead of OOM-crashing.
- **Repair path**: a tool/command that rewrites a bloated JSONL, dropping or trimming `custom` ledgers, so users can rescue long-running sessions.

### Workaround for affected users

Copy the JSONL, strip `custom`-type lines (they are not needed to resume the conversation itself), and resume the copy — or start a new session.

# gh-1073: Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash

## Description

## Session file grows unboundedly (12 GiB) → resume fails with `SessionException: Failed to read session`, then Dart VM OOM crash

### Observed (live, 2026-09-29)

A month-long CLI session (`2026-09-07…01a07bce-….jsonl`) grew to **12.4 GiB / 96,776 lines**. Messages themselves are only ~17 MB; 99.9 % of the file is `custom` ledger records:

| customType | records | total | avg |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model_request_summary` | 18,753 | 9.08 GB | ~484 KB |
| `shell_job_registry` | 29,348 | 3.65 GB | ~124 KB |
| `subagent_registry` | 3,588 | 0.5 GB | ~140 KB |

Resuming the session fails:

```
error: failed to open session 01a07bce-…: SessionException: Failed to read session …/2026-09-07…_01a07bce….jsonl
```

and the process then crashes hard:

```
Exhausted heap space, trying to allocate 25575341936 bytes
```

### Root cause

1. **Unbounded append-only ledgers.**
   - `shell_job_registry` (`lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart`, `_persistJobBoard`): every job-board mutation appends a **full snapshot of all job cards** (commands, cwd, log tails). ~29k snapshots over the session lifetime; no cap, no dedup, no rotation.
   - `model_request_summary` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_blobs.dart`): written before **every** model request and embeds a per-message summary of the whole outbound context (`messageCount` reached 1030+). Growth is superlinear: the longer the session, the bigger each record.

2. **Open path reads the whole file into one String.**
   `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart`) calls `fs.readTextFile(filePath)` on the entire JSONL. A 12.4 GiB UTF-8 file becomes a Dart UTF-16 `String` (~25 GB) → heap exhaustion; the wrapped `Failed to read session` error surfaces first, the retry then kills the VM.

   Note: faster/bounded parsing already exists (`SessionParseExecutor` header-only decode for big ledger payloads, `windowed_session_storage.dart`), but it only kicks in **after** the full-file `readTextFile`, so it cannot help here.

### Suggested fix directions

- **Streamed/windowed open**: read the JSONL line-by-line (or in bounded chunks) during open; never materialize the whole file as a single `String`. The header parse already only needs the first line.
- **Cap/rotate ledger records**:
  - `shell_job_registry`: keep only the latest snapshot (supersede prior records, e.g. tombstone/compact or a sidecar), or truncate job card payloads (log tails) before persisting.
  - `model_request_summary`: cap the per-message summary (max messages / max chars), and/or persist it only when the trajectory actually needs replay data.
- **Hard backstop**: refuse to full-read session files above a threshold (e.g. 1–2 GB) with a clear error pointing at a repair/`--shallow` resume path, instead of OOM-crashing.
- **Repair path**: a tool/command that rewrites a bloated JSONL, dropping or trimming `custom` ledgers, so users can rescue long-running sessions.

### Workaround for affected users

Copy the JSONL, strip `custom`-type lines (they are not needed to resume the conversation itself), and resume the copy — or start a new session.

    "description": "## Session file grows unboundedly (12 GiB) → resume fails with `SessionException: Failed to read session`, then Dart VM OOM crash

### Observed (live, 2026-09-29)

A month-long CLI session (`2026-09-07…01a07bce-….jsonl`) grew to **12.4 GiB / 96,776 lines**. Messages themselves are only ~17 MB; 99.9 % of the file is `custom` ledger records:

| customType | records | total | avg |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model_request_summary` | 18,753 | 9.08 GB | ~484 KB |
| `shell_job_registry` | 29,348 | 3.65 GB | ~124 KB |
| `subagent_registry` | 3,588 | 0.5 GB | ~140 KB |

Resuming the session fails:

```
error: failed to open session 01a07bce-…: SessionException: Failed to read session …/2026-09-07…_01a07bce….jsonl
```

and the process then crashes hard:

```
Exhausted heap space, trying to allocate 25575341936 bytes
```

### Root cause

1. **Unbounded append-only ledgers.**
   - `shell_job_registry` (`lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart`, `_persistJobBoard`): every job-board mutation appends a **full snapshot of all job cards** (commands, cwd, log tails). ~29k snapshots over the session lifetime; no cap, no dedup, no rotation.
   - `model_request_summary` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_blobs.dart`): written before **every** model request and embeds a per-message summary of the whole outbound context (`messageCount` reached 1030+). Growth is superlinear: the longer the session, the bigger each record.

2. **Open path reads the whole file into one String.**
   `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart`) calls `fs.readTextFile(filePath)` on the entire JSONL. A 12.4 GiB UTF-8 file becomes a Dart UTF-16 `String` (~25 GB) → heap exhaustion; the wrapped `Failed to read session` error surfaces first, the retry then kills the VM.

   Note: faster/bounded parsing already exists (`SessionParseExecutor` header-only decode for big ledger payloads, `windowed_session_storage.dart`), but it only kicks in **after** the full-file `readTextFile`, so it cannot help here.

### Suggested fix directions

- **Streamed/windowed open**: read the JSONL line-by-line (or in bounded chunks) during open; never materialize the whole file as a single `String`. The header parse already only needs the first line.
- **Cap/rotate ledger records**:
  - `shell_job_registry`: keep only the latest snapshot (supersede prior records, e.g. tombstone/compact or a sidecar), or truncate job card payloads (log tails) before persisting.
  - `model_request_summary`: cap the per-message summary (max messages / max chars), and/or persist it only when the trajectory actually needs replay data.
- **Hard backstop**: refuse to full-read session files above a threshold (e.g. 1–2 GB) with a clear error pointing at a repair/`--shallow` resume path, instead of OOM-crashing.
- **Repair path**: a tool/command that rewrites a bloated JSONL, dropping or trimming `custom` ledgers, so users can rescue long-running sessions.

### Workaround for affected users

Copy the JSONL, strip `custom`-type lines (they are not needed to resume the conversation itself), and resume the copy — or start a new session.

{"content":"### What changed Bounded the session-JSONL growth that grew a month-long session to 12.4 GiB and made open/resume safe for huge files: ledger payloads are capped and deduped at the write site, the full open streams the file in bounded chunks (never one giant `String`) with a 2 GiB hard backstop, and a new `fa session repair` command rewrites bloated JSONLs. This leg fixed the last review leftovers: one analyzer lint and two stale retry-test assertions that still counted the old `readTextFile` open surface (the open now stats + streams, so the counters read `statCalls`). ### Key decisions - `ledger_caps.dart`: 300-char cap on every string field in `shell_job_registry` / `subagent_registry` records + `LedgerSnapshotDeduper` skips byte-identical snapshots at the write site - `model_request_summary`: per-message summaries capped (newest 64 messages / 256 KB budget); older messages degrade to role+chars stubs — record still describes the whole request - `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked`: stat-first, refuse >2 GiB with a named `tooLarge` `SessionException` pointing at windowed resume / `fa session repair`; ranged filesystems get a fully streamed line-scan parse with header-only decode of giant `custom` ledgers (only the latest per `customType` is fully parsed — exactly what resume rehydration reads) - `session_repair.dart` + CLI: drop replay-only ledger types, keep-latest for snapshot registries, conservative (unknown/unparseable lines kept), backup + `--dry-run` ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/session test/trajectory test/task test/cli ``` Full core suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 7960 passed / 16 skipped. The 3 failures in `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` are environmental — the CI shell leaks `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, which the editor correctly refuses to override (all 13 pass with the var unset). A pre-existing glibc heap-corruption abort in the PTY-harness teardown also reproduces on the base commit and is unrelated.

bounded chunks] STREAM --> HDR[header-only decode
of giant custom ledgers] HDR --> LATEST[fully parse latest
record per customType] WRITE[ledger writes] --> CAP[ledger_caps: 300-char field cap] CAP --> DEDUP[skip identical snapshots] REPAIR[fa session repair] --> REWRITE[drop replay-only ledgers
keep-latest registries + backup] ```

# gh-1073: Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash

## Description

## Session file grows unboundedly (12 GiB) → resume fails with `SessionException: Failed to read session`, then Dart VM OOM crash

### Observed (live, 2026-09-29)

A month-long CLI session (`2026-09-07…01a07bce-….jsonl`) grew to **12.4 GiB / 96,776 lines**. Messages themselves are only ~17 MB; 99.9 % of the file is `custom` ledger records:

| customType | records | total | avg |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model_request_summary` | 18,753 | 9.08 GB | ~484 KB |
| `shell_job_registry` | 29,348 | 3.65 GB | ~124 KB |
| `subagent_registry` | 3,588 | 0.5 GB | ~140 KB |

Resuming the session fails:

```
error: failed to open session 01a07bce-…: SessionException: Failed to read session …/2026-09-07…_01a07bce….jsonl
```

and the process then crashes hard:

```
Exhausted heap space, trying to allocate 25575341936 bytes
```

### Root cause

1. **Unbounded append-only ledgers.**
   - `shell_job_registry` (`lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart`, `_persistJobBoard`): every job-board mutation appends a **full snapshot of all job cards** (commands, cwd, log tails). ~29k snapshots over the session lifetime; no cap, no dedup, no rotation.
   - `model_request_summary` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_blobs.dart`): written before **every** model request and embeds a per-message summary of the whole outbound context (`messageCount` reached 1030+). Growth is superlinear: the longer the session, the bigger each record.

2. **Open path reads the whole file into one String.**
   `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart`) calls `fs.readTextFile(filePath)` on the entire JSONL. A 12.4 GiB UTF-8 file becomes a Dart UTF-16 `String` (~25 GB) → heap exhaustion; the wrapped `Failed to read session` error surfaces first, the retry then kills the VM.

   Note: faster/bounded parsing already exists (`SessionParseExecutor` header-only decode for big ledger payloads, `windowed_session_storage.dart`), but it only kicks in **after** the full-file `readTextFile`, so it cannot help here.

### Suggested fix directions

- **Streamed/windowed open**: read the JSONL line-by-line (or in bounded chunks) during open; never materialize the whole file as a single `String`. The header parse already only needs the first line.
- **Cap/rotate ledger records**:
  - `shell_job_registry`: keep only the latest snapshot (supersede prior records, e.g. tombstone/compact or a sidecar), or truncate job card payloads (log tails) before persisting.
  - `model_request_summary`: cap the per-message summary (max messages / max chars), and/or persist it only when the trajectory actually needs replay data.
- **Hard backstop**: refuse to full-read session files above a threshold (e.g. 1–2 GB) with a clear error pointing at a repair/`--shallow` resume path, instead of OOM-crashing.
- **Repair path**: a tool/command that rewrites a bloated JSONL, dropping or trimming `custom` ledgers, so users can rescue long-running sessions.

### Workaround for affected users

Copy the JSONL, strip `custom`-type lines (they are not needed to resume the conversation itself), and resume the copy — or start a new session.
